name: RAPTOR

paper.title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval

stages.ingestion: The corpus is split into ~100-token chunks without cutting sentences.
stages.construction: Chunks are embedded with SBERT (multi-qa-mpnet-base-cos-v1); GMM soft clustering over UMAP-reduced embeddings (BIC chooses cluster count) groups them and gpt-3.5-turbo summarises each cluster, recursively.
stages.organization: Multi-layer tree: raw chunks as leaves, cluster summaries as parent nodes.
stages.retrieval: Collapsed-tree retrieval (cosine top-k over all nodes of all layers up to a token budget) or tree traversal (top-k per layer from root down); collapsed tree performed better.
stages.answer: Retrieved node texts are concatenated as context for the reader LLM.

summary: Builds a tree of recursive cluster summaries over document chunks and retrieves across all abstraction levels.
notes: AXES-CHECK: leaf nodes are the original 100-token chunks kept verbatim and are retrievable alongside summaries, so 'text kept as: rewritten' understates it (fidelity tag set to verbatim+derived). Evaluated on NarrativeQA, QASPER, QuALITY (document QA); no conversational-memory benchmark, so no results file was written. Code URL not read in the paper text (known official repo).
